SELECT * FROM json_populate_recordset(null::bridging.notes, '[{"id":"019fa77d-8469-7104-aa43-56df5a5cb8fe","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a0-71cf-9863-4d6d67e42e6d","subtopic_name":"Prime factorisation, HCF and LCM","summary":"Express numbers as products of primes in index form, then read HCF from shared primes at lowest powers and LCM from every prime at highest powers.","key_concepts":["A prime is greater than 1 and divisible only by itself and 1","HCF: common bases only, take the lowest power of each","LCM: every prime that appears, take the highest power of each","For a perfect square (cube), every prime power in the factorisation must be divisible by 2 (3)"],"formulas":[{"note":"Ignore primes that appear in only one number.","label":"HCF from primes","expression":"HCF = product of shared primes at lowest powers"},{"note":"Include primes found in only one of the numbers.","label":"LCM from primes","expression":"LCM = product of all primes at highest powers"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["560 = 2^4 x 5 x 7 and 168 = 2^3 x 3 x 7","Shared primes: 2 and 7","Lowest powers: 2^3 and 7","HCF = 2^3 x 7 = 56"],"answer":"56","question":"Find the HCF of 168 and 560."},{"steps":["2700 = 2^2 x 3^3 x 5^2","For a square, every power must be divisible by 2; only 3^3 needs one more factor of 3, so h = 3","For a cube, every power must be divisible by 3; need 2^1 and 5^1 more, so k = 2 x 5 = 10"],"answer":"2700 = 2^2 x 3^3 x 5^2; h = 3; k = 10","question":"Express 2700 as a product of primes. Find the smallest h so that 2700h is a perfect square, and the smallest k so that 2700k is a perfect cube."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"HCF uses the lowest shared powers. Highest powers are for LCM.","mistake":"Taking the highest powers when finding the HCF."},{"fix":"LCM must include every prime that appears in either number.","mistake":"Leaving out a prime that appears in only one number when finding the LCM."}],"exam_tips":["Write both numbers in index form before comparing primes.","For square/cube questions, check which powers are not divisible by 2 or 3, then multiply by the missing factors."],"related_topic_codes":["t04"],"order_index":101,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:50:48.807Z"},{"id":"019fa77d-846f-77df-b73d-aeca15ab2712","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a0-71cf-9863-4d6d67e42e6d","subtopic_name":"Indices and standard form","summary":"Index laws let you simplify powers without expanding. Standard form keeps very large or small numbers as A x 10^n with 1 <= A < 10.","key_concepts":["Same base: multiply by adding indices, divide by subtracting, and raise a power by multiplying indices","a^(-n) = 1/a^n and a^0 = 1 (a != 0)","Fractional indices are roots: a^(m/n) is the nth root of a^m","Standard form is A x 10^n where 1 <= A < 10"],"formulas":[{"note":"Bases must match for the first two laws.","label":"Core index laws","expression":"a^m x a^n = a^(m+n); a^m / a^n = a^(m-n); (a^m)^n = a^(mn)"},{"note":"Neither law applies when a = 0.","label":"Negative and zero index","expression":"a^(-n) = 1/a^n; a^0 = 1"},{"note":"Also (ab)^n = a^n b^n and (a/b)^m = a^m / b^m.","label":"Fractional index","expression":"a^(m/n) = (nth root of a)^m"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Apply (ab)^n = a^n b^n and a^(m/n) as a root: (4x^2)^(3/2) = 4^(3/2) x (x^2)^(3/2)","4^(3/2) = (sqrt(4))^3 = 2^3 = 8","(x^2)^(3/2) = x^(2 x 3/2) = x^3"],"answer":"8x^3","question":"Simplify (4x^2)^(3/2)."},{"steps":["8^0 = 1","(1/2)^(-4) = (2/1)^4 = 16","16 x 1 = 16"],"answer":"16","question":"Evaluate (1/2)^(-4) x 8^0."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"A negative index flips into a reciprocal; it does not change the sign.","mistake":"Treating a negative index as making the answer negative."},{"fix":"The first part must satisfy 1 <= A < 10, so write 3.4 x 10^6.","mistake":"Leaving standard form as 34 x 10^5."}],"exam_tips":["Rewrite nested roots and brackets fully in index form before simplifying from the inside out.","Spot zero powers early; they often collapse a messy expression to 1."],"related_topic_codes":["t04"],"order_index":102,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:50:48.807Z"},{"id":"019fa797-96d3-7fe3-9af0-0623a57032f0","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a0-71cf-9863-4d6d67e42e6d","subtopic_name":"Significant figures, decimal places and estimation","summary":"Significant figures count from the first non-zero digit. Estimation checks whether an answer is a sensible size.","key_concepts":["Count significant figures from the first non-zero digit onwards","Leading zeros are never significant, but trailing zeros after a decimal point are","Decimal places are counted from the decimal point, regardless of zeros","Keep full accuracy through the working and round only at the final step"],"formulas":[{"note":"A quick way to confirm your exact answer is the right size.","label":"Estimation check","expression":"round each value to 1 significant figure, then calculate"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["0.0085: the leading zeros are not significant, so only the 8 and 5 count","20007: the zeros sit between non-zero digits, so all five digits count","12.000: trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant, so all five count"],"answer":"2, 5 and 5 significant figures","question":"State the number of significant figures in 0.0085, 20007 and 12.000."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Start counting at the first non-zero digit, giving 2 significant figures.","mistake":"Counting the leading zeros in 0.0085 as significant figures."},{"fix":"Trailing zeros after a decimal point show the accuracy and must be kept.","mistake":"Dropping the trailing zeros when writing 12.000."},{"fix":"Keep the full value in your calculator and round only the final answer.","mistake":"Rounding partway through a multi-step calculation."}],"exam_tips":["Check whether the question asks for significant figures or decimal places, they are not the same.","If the question does not specify, give money to 2 decimal places and other answers to 3 significant figures."],"related_topic_codes":["t04"],"order_index":103,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:19:17.458Z"},{"id":"019fa77d-846f-7886-a96c-1af51559f12c","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-77cc-bb88-40ce254805a8","subtopic_name":"Ratio and proportional sharing","summary":"Ratios compare parts. Convert a ratio into total parts before sharing an amount.","key_concepts":["Ratios have no units and should be simplified","Total parts = sum of all ratio numbers","One part = total amount divided by total parts"],"formulas":[{"note":"Always find the value of one part first.","label":"Sharing in a ratio","expression":"share = (its part / total parts) x total amount"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Let the numbers be x and 4x","After the change: (x - 5) and (4x + 10)","So (x - 5) / (4x + 10) = 1/6","6x - 30 = 4x + 10, so 2x = 40"],"answer":"20 yellow balls","question":"A bag has yellow and blue balls in the ratio 1:4. Five yellow are removed and 10 blue added, giving a new ratio 1:6. Find the original number of yellow balls."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"A ratio only gives proportions. Find the value of one part first.","mistake":"Treating a ratio number as the actual quantity."},{"fix":"Convert both quantities to the same unit, then simplify.","mistake":"Forgetting to simplify units before writing a ratio."}],"exam_tips":["Set unknowns as x and 4x rather than two separate letters.","Check your answer satisfies the original ratio."],"related_topic_codes":["t06"],"order_index":201,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:50:48.807Z"},{"id":"019fa77d-846f-78a5-8c08-d120beccd3ac","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-77cc-bb88-40ce254805a8","subtopic_name":"Direct and inverse proportion","summary":"Direct proportion means y = kx. Inverse proportion means y = k/x (or y = k over a power/root of x).","key_concepts":["Direct: as one quantity increases, the other increases and y = bx for a constant b","Inverse: as one quantity increases, the other decreases and y = b/x","Find the constant from the given pair first, then substitute the new value"],"formulas":[{"note":"b is the constant of proportionality.","label":"Direct proportion","expression":"y = bx"},{"note":"Also used with roots or powers, e.g. L = b / sqrt(M).","label":"Inverse proportion","expression":"y = b / x"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["y = bx so 144 = b(12), giving b = 12","When x = 7: y = 12 x 7 = 84"],"answer":"84","question":"y is directly proportional to x. Given y = 144 when x = 12, find y when x = 7."},{"steps":["L = b / sqrt(M)","35 = b / 10, so b = 350","700 = 350 / sqrt(M), so sqrt(M) = 1/2 and M = 1/4"],"answer":"M = 1/4","question":"L is inversely proportional to sqrt(M). When M = 100, L = 35. Find M when L = 700."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Always substitute the given pair to find b before answering.","mistake":"Skipping the step of finding the constant."},{"fix":"Inverse means y = b/x (or b over the stated expression).","mistake":"Using y = bx when the question says inversely proportional."}],"exam_tips":["Underline whether the question says directly or inversely proportional.","Label given and new values clearly so the constant step is easy to check."],"related_topic_codes":["t05"],"order_index":202,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:50:48.807Z"},{"id":"019fa797-96d4-7159-960a-e7b03b810be6","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-77cc-bb88-40ce254805a8","subtopic_name":"Speed, distance and travel graphs","summary":"Speed links distance and time. On a travel graph the gradient gives speed and the area can give distance.","key_concepts":["Average speed uses total distance and total time, never the average of two speeds","On a distance-time graph the gradient is the speed","On a speed-time graph the area under the graph is the distance travelled","A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means the object is stationary"],"formulas":[{"note":"Rearranges to distance = speed x time.","label":"Speed","expression":"speed = distance / time"},{"note":"Never average the individual speeds.","label":"Average speed","expression":"average speed = total distance / total time"},{"note":"Multiply by 3.6 to convert m/s into km/h.","label":"Unit conversion","expression":"1 m/s = 3.6 km/h"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["First stage time = 60 / 40 = 1.5 hours","Second stage time = 60 / 60 = 1 hour","Total distance = 120 km and total time = 2.5 hours","Average speed = 120 / 2.5"],"answer":"48 km/h, not 50 km/h","question":"A car travels 60 km at 40 km/h, then a further 60 km at 60 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Average speed is total distance over total time, which gives 48 km/h.","mistake":"Averaging the two speeds to get 50 km/h."},{"fix":"On a distance-time graph the speed is the gradient. The area has no meaning.","mistake":"Finding the area under a distance-time graph."},{"fix":"Convert to consistent units before substituting.","mistake":"Mixing units, such as distance in km with time in minutes."}],"exam_tips":["Write down what each axis shows before reading any travel graph.","For average speed, work out total distance and total time separately first."],"related_topic_codes":["t05"],"order_index":203,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:19:17.458Z"},{"id":"019fa797-96d4-7182-967a-27541bebc955","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-77cc-bb88-40ce254805a8","subtopic_name":"Map scales and scale drawings","summary":"A map scale compares map length to actual length. Areas scale by the square of the length scale.","key_concepts":["Scale = D_map / D_actual, often rewritten as the representative fraction 1 : n","Both lengths must use the same unit before writing 1 : n","A_map / A_actual = (D_map / D_actual)^2"],"formulas":[{"note":"Reduce so the map side is 1.","label":"Length scale","expression":"scale = D_map / D_actual = 1 / n"},{"note":"Square the length scale factor.","label":"Area scale","expression":"A_map / A_actual = (D_map / D_actual)^2"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["1 cm represents 200000 cm = 2 km, so n = 2","Actual distance = 18.9 x 2 = 37.8 km","1 cm^2 represents 2^2 = 4 km^2, so map area = 728.6 / 4 = 182.15 cm^2"],"answer":"n = 2; 37.8 km; 182.15 cm^2","question":"A map has scale 1 : 200000. (a) Write as 1 cm : n km. (b) Map distance 18.9 cm. Find actual distance in km. (c) Actual area 728.6 km^2. Find map area in cm^2."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Square the length scale: areas scale by n^2.","mistake":"Using the length scale factor directly for an area."},{"fix":"Convert both lengths to the same unit before simplifying.","mistake":"Writing 1 : n with mixed units."}],"exam_tips":["Convert 1 : n into a convenient unit pair (e.g. 1 cm : 2 km) before area work.","Check whether the question asks for length or area; that decides whether you square."],"related_topic_codes":["t10"],"order_index":204,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:19:17.458Z"},{"id":"019fa77d-846f-78bf-9be6-38293f247790","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7839-8287-1e75e9dd37f8","subtopic_name":"Percentage change, profit and loss","summary":"Percentages are fractions with denominator 100. Most exam marks come from choosing the correct 100% baseline and using multipliers.","key_concepts":["Percent rate x base value = percentage amount","Increase uses (100% + rate); decrease uses (100% - rate)","Reverse percentage: final value is a known percent of the original, so divide by that multiplier"],"formulas":[{"note":"E.g. 8.5% of $7.20 is GST tax.","label":"Percentage of a base","expression":"amount = rate x base"},{"note":"Always measure against the previous (original) value.","label":"Percentage change","expression":"change / previous value x 100%"},{"note":"For reverse percentages, divide final by that multiplier.","label":"Increase / decrease multiplier","expression":"final = base x (100% +/- rate)"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["$17.50 is 85% of the original price","Original = 17.50 / 0.85 = 20.588...","Round to nearest cent"],"answer":"$20.59","question":"A pair of shoes costs $17.50 after a 15% discount. Find the price before discount."},{"steps":["Previous value = 1298 - 31 = 1267","Percentage increase = 31 / 1267 x 100% = 2.4467...%"],"answer":"2.45%","question":"An index rises from 1267 to 1298 (a change of +31). Find the percentage increase to 3 s.f."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Divide by 0.85. Reverse percentages divide by the remaining percent.","mistake":"Multiplying by 1.15 to reverse a 15% discount."},{"fix":"Percentage change is always measured against the previous value.","mistake":"Using the new value as the 100% baseline for percentage change."}],"exam_tips":["Write down what represents 100% before calculating.","On a calculator, key fraction x 100 (not x 100%) when converting to a percentage."],"related_topic_codes":["t01"],"order_index":301,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:50:48.807Z"},{"id":"019fa77d-846f-78da-8d36-a3c6c5093e2d","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7839-8287-1e75e9dd37f8","subtopic_name":"Simple and compound interest","summary":"Simple interest adds a fixed amount each period on the original principal. Compound interest recalculates on the new balance each period.","key_concepts":["Simple interest per period is constant and based on the original principal","Compound interest amount grows each period because interest is earned on the previous total","Compound formulas usually give the final amount A; interest earned is A - P"],"formulas":[{"note":"R is the rate as a decimal or percent/100; T is the number of periods.","label":"Simple interest","expression":"I = PRT; A = P(1 + RT)"},{"note":"A is the final amount after T compounding periods.","label":"Compound amount","expression":"A = P(1 + r/100)^T"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["I = 2300 x 0.03 x 2 = 138","A = 2300 + 138 = 2438 (or A = 2300(1 + 0.03 x 2))"],"answer":"Interest $138; amount $2438","question":"Deposit $2300 at 3% simple interest per year. Find the interest and amount after 2 years."},{"steps":["After 1 year: 12000 x 1.04 = 12480","After 2 years: 12000 x 1.04^2 = 12979.20"],"answer":"$12979.20","question":"Deposit $12000 at 4% compound interest per year. Find the amount after 2 years."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Interest earned = final amount minus the principal.","mistake":"Reporting the compound amount when the question asks for the interest."},{"fix":"Compound interest multiplies by (1 + r/100) once per period.","mistake":"Using simple interest when the question says compound."}],"exam_tips":["Check whether the question wants the total amount or just the interest.","For simple interest, A = P(1 + RT) is often faster than finding I first."],"related_topic_codes":["t02"],"order_index":302,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:50:48.807Z"},{"id":"019fa797-96d4-7391-a305-684acbf30080","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7839-8287-1e75e9dd37f8","subtopic_name":"Exchange rates, hire purchase and taxation","summary":"Convert currencies carefully with the given rate, and treat hire purchase as deposit plus all instalments (often with simple interest on the balance).","key_concepts":["Rewrite the exchange rate so the currency you want is on the RHS before multiplying","Hire purchase total = deposit + remaining amount + interest (if charged)","Tax is charged in bands, so only the income inside each band is taxed at that band''s rate"],"formulas":[{"note":"Invert the given rate if needed, then multiply.","label":"Currency conversion","expression":"new amount = original amount x (units of new per 1 unit of old)"},{"note":"Total payable = deposit + remaining amount + interest.","label":"Hire purchase instalment","expression":"instalment = (remaining amount + total interest) / number of instalments"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["1 EUR = 1/0.64 = 1.5625 SGD","30 EUR = 30 x 1.5625 = 46.875 SGD","Total = 46.875 + 7 = 53.875 SGD"],"answer":"53.88 SGD (2 d.p.)","question":"1 SGD = 0.64 EUR. A present costs 19 EUR + 11 EUR transport, plus 7 SGD import charges. Find the total in SGD."},{"steps":["Deposit = 0.4 x 50000 = 20000; remaining = 30000","Interest = 30000 x 0.025 = 750","Monthly instalment = (30000 + 750) / 24 = 1281.25","Total payable = 20000 + 30000 + 750 = 50750"],"answer":"$1281.25 per month; total $50750","question":"A car costs $50000. Deposit 40%, then 24 monthly instalments with 2.5% simple interest on the remaining amount. Find the monthly instalment and total payable."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Sanity-check the size, or rewrite the rate so the target currency is on the RHS.","mistake":"Multiplying when you should divide in a currency conversion."},{"fix":"Total = deposit + remaining balance + interest charged.","mistake":"Forgetting the deposit or the interest when totalling hire purchase."},{"fix":"Only the part of the income inside a band is taxed at that band''s rate.","mistake":"Taxing the whole income at the highest band rate."}],"exam_tips":["Write the exchange rate as a fraction and cancel units.","Hire purchase always costs at least as much as cash (usually more); use that as a check."],"related_topic_codes":["t01"],"order_index":303,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:19:17.458Z"},{"id":"019fa77e-4a20-77c9-9dbd-84e3b0a7ecaf","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7853-96ff-2c02dc5e1f10","subtopic_name":"Expansion and factorisation","summary":"Expand by multiplying every term; factorise by extracting common factors or recognising identities. Only like terms can be combined.","key_concepts":["Only like terms can be added or subtracted (e.g. 2x + 3x = 5x)","Expand by multiplying the outside term (or each term) through every term in the bracket","Factorisation reverses expansion: take out the HCF, use identities, grouping, or the cross method"],"formulas":[{"note":"Spot these before using the general rainbow/FOIL method.","label":"Perfect square and difference of squares","expression":"(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2; (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2; a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["(3x + 5)^2 = 9x^2 + 2(3x)(5) + 25 = 9x^2 + 30x + 25","(x + 5)(x - 5) = x^2 - 25"],"answer":"9x^2 + 30x + 25; x^2 - 25","question":"Expand (3x + 5)^2 and (x + 5)(x - 5)."},{"steps":["49 - 4x^2 = 7^2 - (2x)^2 = (7 - 2x)(7 + 2x)","2a^2 - 8a = 2a(a - 4)"],"answer":"(7 - 2x)(7 + 2x); 2a(a - 4)","question":"Factorise completely 49 - 4x^2 and 2a^2 - 8a."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Include the middle term 2ab.","mistake":"Writing (a + b)^2 as a^2 + b^2."},{"fix":"Only like terms (same letters and powers) can be added or subtracted.","mistake":"Combining unlike terms such as 3x and 5."}],"exam_tips":["Expand your factorised answer mentally to check it.","Completely usually means take out a common factor and then factorise further."],"related_topic_codes":["t06"],"order_index":401,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:51:39.424Z"},{"id":"019fa77e-4a20-7a03-898c-3b69d3499409","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7853-96ff-2c02dc5e1f10","subtopic_name":"Algebraic fractions and changing the subject","summary":"Combine algebraic fractions over a common denominator, and rearrange formulas so the required letter stands alone on the LHS.","key_concepts":["Factorise denominators before finding a common denominator; cancel factors only","Changing the subject means isolating one letter alone on the LHS","Square roots give +/- answers unless the context (e.g. distance) rejects the negative"],"formulas":[{"note":"Simplify the result if possible.","label":"Adding fractions","expression":"a/b + c/d = (ad + bc) / bd"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Divide both sides by m: E/m = c^2","Square root both sides: c = +/- sqrt(E/m)"],"answer":"c = +/- sqrt(E/m)","question":"Make c the subject of E = mc^2."},{"steps":["Multiply both sides by 2: 2E = mv^2","Divide by v^2: m = 2E / v^2"],"answer":"m = 2E / v^2","question":"Make m the subject of E = (1/2)mv^2."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Only cancel a factor common to the whole numerator and denominator.","mistake":"Cancelling the x in (x + 3)/x."},{"fix":"Include both signs unless the question rejects negatives (e.g. length).","mistake":"Dropping the +/- when taking a square root in changing the subject."}],"exam_tips":["Undo operations in reverse order: clear fractions, isolate the powered term, then take roots.","When the new subject appears twice, collect those terms and factorise it out."],"related_topic_codes":["t06"],"order_index":402,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:51:39.424Z"},{"id":"019fa798-94cc-7fb5-ade9-4a1dcec6c8f9","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7853-96ff-2c02dc5e1f10","subtopic_name":"Number patterns and the nth term","summary":"A linear sequence increases by the same amount each time, and its nth term takes the form an + b.","key_concepts":["The common difference is the amount added each time and becomes the coefficient of n","Check your nth term by substituting n = 1 to see if it gives the first term","The nth term lets you jump straight to any term without listing them all","A decreasing sequence has a negative common difference"],"formulas":[{"note":"a is the common difference and b adjusts the first term.","label":"Linear sequence","expression":"T_n = an + b"},{"note":"Because T_1 = a + b.","label":"Finding b","expression":"b = first term - a"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["The common difference is 3, so a = 3","b = first term - a = 5 - 3 = 2","So T_n = 3n + 2","T_20 = 3(20) + 2"],"answer":"T_n = 3n + 2 and the 20th term is 62","question":"Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and hence find the 20th term."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"3n alone gives 3, 6, 9.
